longDescription: The Phono Museum showcases the fascinating history of sound recording and playback. Experience in AR how historic phonographs and gramophones worked.
quizIntroTitle: Sound Quiz at the Phono Museum
quizIntroDescription: Listen carefully to each sound and match it to the right medium. You can retry every question as often as you like - this is about learning and having fun.
feedbackCorrectBody: Nice one - that was the correct medium.
feedbackWrongBody: Good try. Now you can see the correct medium.
dragInstruction: Drag across the cube to rotate
finishFailure: You can continue and complete the station now.
completionBlockedHint: Take the quiz at your own pace and complete the station afterwards.
arStartDescription: Tap start to allow motion and orientation access for gyroscope controls.

mediumLesson.title: Sound Training Before the Quiz
mediumLesson.subtitle: Listen to all three media first and learn how their sound signatures differ.
mediumLesson.resultBody: You answered {correct} of {total} training questions correctly.

questions.prompt: Which medium sounds the most muffled, with an audible crackle in the background?
questions.explanation: The phonograph plays early wax cylinders. That is why it sounds dull and warm, with a faint crackle and hiss in the background.

questions.prompt: Which medium sounds strong and a bit tinny, as if coming from a horn?
questions.explanation: The gramophone plays the sound through a large horn. That makes it sound strong and a little tinny.

questions.prompt: Which medium sounds the clearest and most modern?
questions.explanation: The turntable sounds clearer and fuller than the older devices.

yourTurn.title: Your turn
yourTurn.subtitle: Build your own melody with 6 to 8 notes and hear it played by different media.
yourTurn.melodyHint: Select at least 6 and at most 8 notes.
yourTurn.requiredPlayHint: Tip: Play your melody once with a medium to compare tonal character.

questions.prompt: Which medium plays this first sound clip?
questions.soundExplanation: The phonograph sounds dull and scratchy because the wax cylinder only captures a smaller range of tones and the fine, high notes get lost.

questions.prompt: Which medium can be heard in the second clip?
questions.soundExplanation: The record player sounds clearer and fuller because vinyl can store more detail and reproduces both quiet and loud notes better.

questions.prompt: Which medium is playing in the third clip?
questions.soundExplanation: The gramophone sounds strong and a bit tinny because the sound is mechanically amplified through a large horn.
